solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Start to generate a little illumination (8)

indicators.note: the start of a word is where it begins, so only the opening letter of 'generate' is used

annotation.surface: Someone coaxing a faint glow into life, perhaps striking a match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start to generate' reads as an instruction to switch something on; it only wants one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: lamps burning coal gas lit Victorian streets, one historic form of illumination.

entries.clue: Feeling angst about embracing hardcore rapper (7)

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so these words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the last letter of 'Feeling' to the first of 'about'

annotation.surface: A tough rapper whose swagger hides anxiety.
annotation.walkthrough: 'angst about' looks like an anagram of ANGST, but the answer sits whole across three words: G from the end of feeling, then angst, then the A of about.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: gangsta rap is a hardcore hip-hop style, and its performers are called gangstas.

entries.clue: Samuel and couple from Bath dance (5)

indicators.note: a couple is a pair, so take two letters from the front of 'Bath'

blocks.note: the usual short form of the name Samuel

annotation.surface: Samuel and his partner from the spa town of Bath take to the dance floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like two dancers from Bath, an English spa city; it means two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the lively Brazilian carnival dance is one kind of dance.

entries.clue: Content to join them, one year, enjoying wealth (2,3,5)

blocks.note: the contents of something are in it

annotation.surface: Someone happy to join a group for a year while living in comfort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as happy; here it is the noun, what a container holds, which is inside.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone in the money has plenty of cash, so is enjoying wealth.

entries.clue: African scavengers laugh about hunger strike primarily (6)

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around: the laugh goes around the hunger
primarily means first of all, so 'strike' gives its first letter

blocks.note: a yen is a longing, a hunger

annotation.surface: Laughing hyenas are pictured as scavengers ready to strike when hungry.
annotation.walkthrough: Hyenas are famous for their laughing call, so 'laugh' belongs in the scene as well as in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: spotted and striped hyenas live in Africa and feed largely on carcasses.

entries.clue: Just beautiful (4)

blocks.note: the old poetic sense, as in a maiden of the ballads

annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' pretends to be the adverb, as in merely beautiful; it is the adjective meaning even-handed.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms both ways: fair means just (a fair ruling) and, in older poetic use, beautiful (fair lady).

entries.clue: Country song engages roughly half the population (7)

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or occupy, so the song takes the men into its middle

blocks.note: an aria is an operatic song
men make up about half of any population

annotation.surface: A national song that appeals to about half the country's people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country song' looks like a single idea, a music genre; the break comes after 'Country'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Armenia is a nation in the Caucasus, between Turkey and Azerbaijan.

entries.clue: Actual beginning of Mongol Empire (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so 'Mongol' gives one letter

annotation.surface: The true origins of the Mongol Empire.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Mongol Empire' as one name; 'Empire' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a realm is the territory a monarch rules, which an empire also is.

entries.clue: It’s unimportant what characterises a vacuum (2,6)

blocks.note: the everyday phrase for shrugging something off
the physics: a vacuum is space empty of any substance

annotation.walkthrough: The second half is literally true: a vacuum is defined by having nothing in it, and 'matter' is the physicist's word for substance.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom and a literal phrase: 'no matter' shrugs off something unimportant, and in physics a vacuum holds no matter.

entries.clue: Initially, Forster may cut novel (4)

indicators.note: initials are the first letters of a name, and Forster signed himself E. M.
something cut is cut short, so 'may' loses its last letter

blocks.note: E. M. Forster, the novelist, by his initials

annotation.surface: Forster might trim a novel in its early draft.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is Jane Austen's novel, not Forster's, which the surface quietly hopes you will not notice.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Jane Austen's 1815 novel about a matchmaking heroine.

entries.clue: Subsequently going through ordeal with three participants (10)

indicators.note: to go through something is to pass inside it, so 'subsequently' sits within the ordeal

annotation.surface: Someone later enduring a three-way ordeal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'going through ordeal' reads as suffering; it is the placing instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym from Latin: tri- (three) and lateral (sides), so talks with three parties are trilateral.

entries.clue: Meagre score in skittles (5)

blocks.note: lean, scanty, as in a thin frame or a frugal meal
felling all the pins with two balls rather than one

annotation.surface: A poor score in a game of skittles.
annotation.walkthrough: Skittles is the British pub game of bowling at pins; the scoring term is actually a good result, not a meagre one.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym plus a sports term: spare means meagre (a spare diet), and in bowling a spare is two balls felling all pins.

entries.clue: In the morning, catching companion opening letters? (7)

indicators.note: to catch is to take hold of, so the morning holds the companion inside it

blocks.note: a crony is a close companion

annotation.surface: Someone opening the post first thing with a friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'opening letters' pictures the morning mail; the question mark flags that it means initial letters forming a word.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist: the opening letters of a phrase, like NATO or radar, make up the kind of word asked for.

entries.clue: A puzzle mostly concerning part of South America (6)

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

annotation.surface: A puzzle largely about South American geography.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A puzzle' looks like the crossword itself; the puzzle meant is a maze.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the great river basin and rainforest covering much of northern South America.

entries.clue: Okay, state how old you are (7)

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: Someone told it's fine to say how old they are.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Okay' reads as permission; it is the adjective meaning middling, and 'state' is the verb, not a nation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an okay performance is an average one, neither good nor bad.

entries.clue: Pack animal roughly east of mountain area (6)

indicators.note: in an across clue east is to the right, so 'roughly' is written after 'mountain area'

annotation.surface: A pack animal found somewhere to the east of the mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'roughly' seems to hedge the geography; it is the abbreviation for circa.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: alpacas are Andean camelids, related to llamas, that can carry light loads.

entries.clue: Two-star novel — no less than that (2,5)

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made into something new

annotation.surface: A reviewer giving a novel two stars, and insisting it deserves no less.
annotation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being rated; it is the adjective meaning new.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'at worst' names the floor of an estimate, so the result will be no less than that.

entries.clue: Run of luck confused skater (6)

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters of 'skater' are muddled

annotation.surface: A skater, dazed after a run of good fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' sits next to a skater and suggests a sprint across the ice; the definition is the whole phrase 'Run of luck'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a winning streak is an unbroken run of luck.

entries.clue: Constantly established high point (7)

blocks.note: the abbreviation est., as in 'est. 1850' on shop signs

annotation.surface: A peak that has always stood firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'high point' reads as a highlight; it is literal, the world's tallest mountain.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the highest mountain on Earth, and by extension any peak of achievement.

entries.clue: Rising trend to accept Conservative decree (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top
to accept is to take in, so the reversed trend takes the Conservative inside it

blocks.note: the tide of opinion is its trend

annotation.surface: A political shift that brings in a Conservative ruling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising trend' reads as a growing fashion; 'Rising' only turns the word upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an edict is an official decree issued by authority.

entries.clue: Cast finished broadcast (5)

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

annotation.surface: The cast of a show has finished its broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the actors; it is the past tense of the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cast and threw are both past tenses of verbs meaning to fling.

entries.clue: Wanders through woods without leader (5)

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, and 'without' removes it

annotation.surface: Someone wandering through woods, leaderless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'woods' must first become a synonym before it loses its head.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rove is to wander aimlessly.

entries.clue: Existential statement has at first mystified prayer leader (4)

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so the statement holds the letter
at first means the opening letter of 'mystified'

blocks.note: 'I am', the simplest statement of existence

annotation.surface: A prayer leader baffled by a philosophical claim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Existential statement' sounds like philosophy; it is just the two words claiming existence, as in 'I think, therefore I am'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in a mosque the imam leads the congregation in prayer.

entries.clue: Pirate finished after char (3,5)

indicators.note: after means following, so 'finished' is written following 'char'

annotation.surface: A pirate done for once he'd been burned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'char' can be British slang for tea or a charwoman; here it is the verb, to scorch.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive synonym: a pirate roams the seas, so an old word for one is a sea rover.

entries.clue: Three attempt taking ecstasy (4)

indicators.note: taking in the sense of taking on board, so the attempt holds the drug inside it

annotation.surface: Three people trying drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Three' at the start reads as a number of people; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist word: in cards and dice, the three-spot is called a trey.

entries.clue: Range of capabilities initially seen in piece of cookware (5,3)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of 'seen' is used
in means placed inside, so the letter goes into the cookware

blocks.note: a skillet is a frying pan

annotation.surface: Someone showing their range as a cook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' tempts you towards the kitchen stove, which suits the cookware; it means scope.
annotation.definitionFit: A modern compound: the set of skills a person has is their range of capabilities.
